summary: Segmented node2 and node3 onto separate VLANs (10 and 20) over the shared link (node1 eth1 / node2 enp8s0 / node3 enp8s0), with node1 (VyOS) routing between them via 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24). node2 got enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24) via NetworkManager VLAN connection 'vlan10', node3 got enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24) via 'vlan20'. Static routes to the peer VLAN subnet were added on node2/node3 (via node1's VLAN gateway) with never-default so the low-metric management-network default route doesn't hijack inter-VLAN traffic. Verified cross-VLAN ping success and confirmed via tcpdump on node1's eth1 that traffic is genuinely 802.1Q-tagged (vlan 10 / vlan 20) end to end. All configs are persistent (VyOS 'save', NetworkManager connections with autoconnect). Completed the mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time), each confirmed via a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, with VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN ping verified healthy after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline network config on node1 (VyOS), node2 (RHEL9), node3 (RHEL9)
Configured VyOS node1 with 802.1Q VLAN sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24), set forward filter default-action accept, committed and saved
Configured node2 with NetworkManager VLAN connection 'vlan10' on enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24, VLAN ID 10)
Configured node3 with NetworkManager VLAN connection 'vlan20' on enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24, VLAN ID 20)

Diagnosed and fixed a default-route metric conflict causing inter-VLAN pings to fail by setting ipv4.never-default and adding explicit static routes to the peer subnet via node1's VLAN gateway on both node2 and node3
Verified bidirectional cross-VLAN ping between node2 and node3
Captured tcpdump evidence on node1 eth1 proving genuine 802.1Q VLAN tagging (vlan 10 / vlan 20) for the routed ICMP traffic
Captured boot_id and service-health baselines on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3, polling each until command execution resumed
Verified changed boot_id and full recovery (VLAN interfaces, routes, cross-VLAN ping) after each individual node restart

evidence.requirement: node2 on VLAN 10, node3 on VLAN 20 over the shared link, with node1 routing between them
evidence.summary: node1 configured with eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24) VLAN sub-interfaces and forwarding enabled; node2 got vlan10 connection on enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24); node3 got vlan20 connection on enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24)

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across VLANs via node1
evidence.summary: Static routes added to route peer-VLAN traffic via node1's VLAN gateway; successful bidirectional ping (0% loss, ttl=63 confirming routed hop) between node2 (10.10.10.11) and node3 (10.10.20.12)

evidence.requirement: traffic is genuinely VLAN-tagged (802.1Q) on the shared link, not just routed by coincidence
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 eth1 shows ICMP echo request/reply tagged 'vlan 10' from node2 and 'vlan 20' from node3, confirming real 802.1Q segmentation

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4098161f..., reboot acknowledged, connection loss confirmed disruption, boot_id changed to f72af8f6... on recovery, VLAN sub-interfaces and forwarding sysctls confirmed intact post-reboot, cross-VLAN ping from node2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5..., reboot acknowledged, connection loss confirmed, boot_id changed to e2f08456... on recovery, VLAN interface/routes intact, successful ping to node3 across VLANs post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f1afbc7f..., reboot acknowledged, connection loss confirmed, boot_id changed to d18e4baf... on recovery, VLAN interface/routes intact, successful ping to node2 across VLANs post-reboot
